facts.claim: Route Handlers: file app/api/ingest/route.ts exporting `async function POST(request: Request|NextRequest)`; body parsed with standard Web API (`await request.json()`, `.text()`, `.formData()`); no bodyParser config needed. Only GET handlers can ever be cached/prerendered; POST is never cached. `params` is a Promise (await it); `RouteContext<'/path/[id]'>` is a global typed helper generated by next dev/build/typegen. Next.js returns 405 for unsupported methods and auto-implements OPTIONS.
facts.verified_how: Fetched route.js reference + getting-started/route-handlers as markdown

facts.claim: Runtime: Route Handlers default to the Node.js runtime. `export const runtime = 'nodejs'` is still accepted without Cache Components but the docs say remove the export; `runtime='edge'` is DEPRECATED. When cacheComponents is enabled, ANY `runtime` export (even 'nodejs') is unsupported and must be removed. `runtime` cannot be used in proxy.ts (Node.js only).
facts.verified_how: Fetched page (lastUpdated 2026-10-15) and proxy docs

facts.claim: cacheComponents defaults to OFF (opt-in: `cacheComponents: true` in next.config, ideally with `partialPrefetching` set explicitly or a warning is logged), BUT create-next-app now scaffolds it ON by default for App Router. With it enabled, route segment configs `dynamic`, `revalidate`, `fetchCache` (and `runtime`) are removed and will ERROR; data is dynamic by default and you opt IN to caching with `use cache` + cacheLife. With it disabled (default), `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` still works and is documented in the 'previous model' guide; v16 only removed those configs when Cache Components is enabled.
facts.verified_how: Read Route Segment Config version history (v16.0.0 row), cacheComponents, create-next-app, migrating-to-cache-components and caching-without-cache-components pages

facts.claim: Forcing dynamic rendering for the public page that reads SQLite: (A) Cache Components OFF: `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` in page.tsx (documented, not deprecated) or `await connection()` from 'next/server' before the query. (B) Cache Components ON: remove `dynamic`; call `await connection()` (or `await io()` from 'next/cache', preferred inside Cache Components since it can be cached/prefetched) before the node:sqlite read AND wrap the component in <Suspense> so the static shell ships. `connection()` replaces unstable_noStore. For GET Route Handlers with CC on, reading request/DB/async IO stops prerender automatically; `use cache` cannot sit directly in a handler body (extract helper).
facts.verified_how: Read connection, io, caching (Cache Components) and route-handlers pages; GitHub issue vercel/next.js#86379 confirms SQLite pages become static at build without these

facts.claim: `middleware.ts` was renamed to `proxy.ts` in Next.js 16: file `proxy.ts` at project root (or src/), named export `proxy` (default export also OK). The `middleware` filename/export is deprecated (still works; edge runtime only available by staying on middleware). Proxy always runs on Node.js runtime, `runtime` config in proxy throws. Without a `matcher` it runs on every request incl. _next/static, images and public/. Codemod: `npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest`. Config flag skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize is now skipProxyUrlNormalize. Proxy buffers request bodies up to 10MB (experimental.proxyClientMaxBodySize).
facts.verified_how: Read proxy.js reference and version-16 upgrade guide

Filesystem caching on by default. `next dev` writes to .next/dev (separate from build output) and uses a lockfile.

facts.claim: HTTP Request 4.5 exact parameter names. Core: `method` (GET, POST, PUT, ...), `url`, `authentication` (none | predefinedCredentialType | genericCredentialType), `genericAuthType` (credential type name, e.g. httpHeaderAuth or httpBearerAuth), `nodeCredentialType` (only for predefined). Body: `sendBody` (boolean), `contentType` (json | form-urlencoded | multipart-form-data | binaryData | raw), `specifyBody` (keypair | json), `jsonBody` (string, usually an expression), `bodyParameters`. Headers: `sendHeaders`, `specifyHeaders`, `headerParameters`, `jsonHeaders`. Options live in `options`. The timeout key is `options.timeout` in ms, min 1, default 10000; it is the time to wait for response headers. Other option keys include `response`, `redirect`, `proxy` and `batching`. Credentials are bound at node level as `"credentials": {"httpHeaderAuth": {"id": "...", "name": "..."}}`.
facts.verified_how: Read HttpRequest/V3/Description.js in the n8n-nodes-base@2.45.3 tarball (names/values and the options.timeout default); WebFetch of the docs page

facts.claim: Node-level settings are top-level keys on the node object, not under parameters: `retryOnFail` (boolean), `maxTries` (number), `waitBetweenTries` (ms), `alwaysOutputData`, `executeOnce`, and `onError` with values `stopWorkflow` | `continueRegularOutput` | `continueErrorOutput`. The legacy `continueOnFail` key still exists in the type. The engine clamps maxTries to 2..5 (default 3) and waitBetweenTries to 0..5000 ms (default 1000). The docs error-handling page does not document these settings, so the source is the authority.
facts.verified_how: Read INode and OnError in n8n-workflow@2.45.1 interfaces.d.ts; read getRetryParams in n8n-core@2.45.3 workflow-execute.js (Math.min(5, Math.max(2, maxTries||3)), Math.min(5000, Math.max(0, waitBetweenTries||1000)))

facts.claim: Header Auth credential: type name `httpHeaderAuth`, display name 'Header Auth'. Fields are `name` (the header name, e.g. Authorization or X-Ingest-Key) and `value` (password-type field; for Authorization it must include the 'Bearer ' prefix). It sends the single header name: value. The alternative `httpBearerAuth` (display name 'Bearer Auth') has the single field `token` and sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Both are genericAuth credentials, so they are valid for `authentication: genericCredentialType`. The docs UI list names 'Header auth', and also 'Simplified Custom Auth' (httpTemplatedCustomAuth), which is the newer option. Plain httpHeaderAuth and httpBearerAuth are still supported.
facts.verified_how: Read HttpHeaderAuth.credentials.js and HttpBearerAuth.credentials.js in the n8n-nodes-base@2.45.3 tarball; the genericAuthType hint text in HttpRequest/V3/Description.js

facts.claim: `n8n import:credentials --input=file.json` expects a JSON ARRAY of credential objects; a bare object is rejected with 'Make sure the credentials are contained in an array'. If an entry's `data` is a plain (decrypted) object, the CLI encrypts it with the instance key (`cipher.encryptV2`) before saving. So plaintext credential JSON is valid input. Flags: --input/-i, --separate, --include, --exclude, --userId, --projectId. The docs page for the CLI does not state this encryption behavior; the source does. Matching `id`s overwrite existing credentials. Use a stable id (1-16 chars) so workflow nodes can reference `credentials.httpHeaderAuth.id`.
facts.verified_how: Read import/credentials.ts at tag n8n@2.45.4 (Array.isArray check ~line 483; 'plain data / decrypted input. Should be encrypted first' -> cipher.encryptV2 ~line 499); WebFetch of the CLI docs page, which is silent on it

facts.claim: `n8n import:workflow --input=file.json` accepts a single workflow object or an array (--separate imports *.json from a directory). The default `--activeState=false` imports every workflow UNPUBLISHED. `--activeState=fromJson` only works in queue/multi-main mode and errors in regular mode. IDs in the file are kept, and a matching id overwrites. Include an `id` in the JSON so the next command can target it. The workflow must reference credentials by `{id, name}` matching an imported credential. Use --projectId or --userId (mutually exclusive) to pick the owner; the default owner is the instance owner.
facts.verified_how: Read import/workflow.ts at tag n8n@2.45.4 (flagsSchema, fromJson guard, readWorkflows array handling); WebFetch of docs.n8n.io/hosting/cli-commands/

facts.claim: Yes: in 2.x 'publish' replaced 'activate'. The editor toggle became Publish/Unpublish buttons. CLI: `n8n publish:workflow --id=<ID> [--versionId=<VID>]` and `n8n unpublish:workflow --id=<ID>|--all`. `publish:workflow --all` was removed. `n8n update:workflow --id=X --active=true` is deprecated and 'will be removed' but still works (it publishes the current version). The docs say changes apply without restart when N8N_USE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_SERVICE is on (default; polls every 15 s), whereas the command's own log text says 'Please restart n8n for changes to take effect if n8n is currently running'. These conflict. Plan on waiting about 15 s, and `docker restart` as a fallback if the trigger does not fire. The external hook `workflow.activeChange` is deprecated in favour of `workflow.published`.
facts.verified_how: WebFetch of docs.n8n.io/hosting/cli-commands/ and /2-0-breaking-changes/; read cli/src/commands/publish/workflow.ts at tag n8n@2.45.4

facts.claim: Public REST API is available on self-hosted at `<host>/api/v1`. Auth is the header `X-N8N-API-KEY` (OpenAPI apiKey scheme; an API key is created in the UI under Settings > n8n API). Workflow endpoints at tag 2.45.4 include createWorkflow (POST /workflows), publishWorkflow (POST /workflows/{workflowId}/publish, body optional {versionId,name,description}, scope workflow:activate) and unpublishWorkflow. `activateWorkflow` (POST /workflows/{workflowId}/activate) and `deactivateWorkflow` still exist but are marked DEPRECATED ('use POST /workflows/{id}/publish instead'). The POST /workflows body requires `name`, `nodes`, `connections` and `settings`; `active`, `id`, `versionId` and `tags` are read-only. POST /credentials takes {name, type, data, ...} and returns the stored credential; `data` is writeOnly. `isApiKeyAuthEnabled()` exists, so key auth can be disabled by config. The API is not available on the free trial.
facts.verified_how: Read openapi.yml (securitySchemes ApiKeyAuth name X-N8N-API-KEY) and handlers/workflows/spec/paths/{createWorkflow,activateWorkflow,publishWorkflow}.generated.yml and handlers/credentials/spec/paths/createCredential.generated.yml at tag n8n@2.45.4; WebFetch of docs.n8n.io/api/. The exact route `/credentials` and `/workflows/{id}/publish` paths are inferred from operationIds and the deprecation text, not from the path-key line.

facts.claim: Apple LaunchAgents doc (archive, 2016): per-user agents live in ~/Library/LaunchAgents (also /Library/LaunchAgents global, /System/Library/LaunchAgents Apple's own). Label and ProgramArguments are the required keys; KeepAlive true = always run; StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath redirect output; per-user plist must be owned by that user and not group/world-writable. The page does not cover RunAtLoad, ProcessType, EnvironmentVariables or launchctl bootstrap; those come from launchd.plist(5) and launchctl(1).

facts.claim: launchd.plist(5) on macOS 27.2: RunAtLoad (bool, default false; man page says it 'should be avoided' for speculative launches, but fine for an agent you want up at login; KeepAlive true also starts the job at load); KeepAlive (bool or dict of conditions, default false; dict supports SuccessfulExit, NetworkState, PathState, etc.); ProcessType values Background | Standard | Adaptive | Interactive (unset = Standard with 'light resource limits' throttling CPU and I/O; Background is the right choice for a metrics agent); EnvironmentVariables (dict of strings only, non-string values ignored); StandardOutPath / StandardErrorPath (file is created if missing); ThrottleInterval default 10 s (restart rate limit); ProgramArguments[0] should be an absolute path (relative is resolved via _PATH_STDPATH, which is minimal), so use the absolute path of node (e.g. /opt/homebrew/bin/node) and set PATH in EnvironmentVariables if needed.

facts.claim: launchctl: 'load' and 'unload' are listed under LEGACY SUBCOMMANDS in launchctl(1) with 'Recommended alternative subcommands: bootstrap | bootout | enable | disable'. Modern flow for a per-user GUI agent: launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist; launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<label> (or bootout with the plist path); launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/<label> to restart; launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/<label> to inspect. gui/<uid> targets the GUI login domain and exists only while the user is logged in at the GUI (use user/<uid> for a domain independent of GUI login). 'bootstrap' fails if the label is already loaded, so bootout first when redeploying. Also 'disable' state persists across boots.
facts.verified_how: man launchctl | col -b on this Mac (macOS 27.2): LEGACY SUBCOMMANDS section, gui/<uid> specifier text, kickstart -kp text. ss64 link is secondary and not relied on.

facts.claim: Lima docs (default user-mode network page): the host's loopback is reachable from the guest as host.lima.internal at 192.168.5.2, including services listening only on the host's 127.0.0.1. Direction is guest->host; the reverse (host->guest ports) is Lima port forwarding, which is separate. Lima 2.3 added networkOpts.hostLoopback: false (vz only, not user-v2) to block this; default stays reachable. Lima issue #5574 (PR #5581 merged 2026-10-16) confirms the default behaviour and the vz-only scope. Installed limactl is 2.2.1, so the option is not available locally yet. Security consequence: any container or the VM can reach every loopback-only service on the Mac (including the metrics agent), so the agent needs its own Bearer token or at least must expose only the allowlisted fields; and if hostLoopback:false is later set, host.lima.internal will be refused and the agent must bind a LAN/all-interface address.

facts.claim: Proxying to a container by name: put Caddy and the Next container on the same user-defined Docker network; Docker's embedded DNS resolves container name (and compose service name/aliases) there ('User-defined bridges provide automatic DNS resolution between containers'; the default bridge does not). Caddyfile: specs.remypost.me { request_body { max_size 64KB } reverse_proxy specs-web:3000 }. Do not publish the Next port on the host. facts.claim: reverse_proxy header defaults: Caddy passes all incoming headers including Host to the backend unmodified, except it sets/augments X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host. Incoming X-Forwarded-* values from clients are IGNORED (anti-spoofing) unless the client IP is in trusted_proxies (configure via global servers > trusted_proxies, not per-proxy; only needed if a CDN/another proxy sits in front, e.g. Cloudflare). Since v2.11.0 Caddy auto-sets Host to upstream host for HTTPS upstreams (not relevant for plain http to a container). Next gets Host: specs.remypost.me and X-Forwarded-For with the real client IP; no header_up needed for the plain-HTTP container case. Defaults: dial_timeout 3s, read_timeout none, lb retries off, response partially buffered, health checks off.
facts.verified_how: Read caddyserver/website src/docs/markdown/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy.md lines 502-545, 613, 621

facts.claim: request_body { max_size <size> } caps incoming body: accepts go-humanize sizes (e.g. 64KB, 1MB), reads beyond the limit fail with HTTP 413. In v2.11.7 source it wraps r.Body with http.MaxBytesReader and maps MaxBytesError to caddyhttp.Error(413); it does NOT pre-check Content-Length, so the 413 arises when the body is read/streamed to the upstream (client may see a reset or 413 depending on how far the proxy got). request_body is in the Caddyfile directive order before reverse_proxy, so it applies when written in the same site block (use handle/route if scoping to /api/ingest: handle /api/ingest { request_body { max_size 64KB } reverse_proxy specs-web:3000 }). Experimental set subdirective exists (v2.10.0+); read_timeout/write_timeout subdirectives were REMOVED from request_body - use the timeouts directive. Also enforce a size/zod limit in the route handler as defense in depth.
facts.verified_how: Read request_body.md and modules/caddyhttp/requestbody/requestbody.go at tag v2.11.7; directives.go order list (request_body line 62, reverse_proxy line 95)
